items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: Well he was a piano leader and he featured himself. And the only time I would get a good crack at it was when he would leave the bandstand like in Hamilton, Ontario.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you one thing before I forget it. Did you take any choruses with Arnold Johnson on the records?

No, never. Just ensemble. Just ensemble. Well he was a piano leader and he featured himself. And the only time I would get a good crack at it was when he would leave the bandstand like in Hamilton, Ontario. He'd go off with the committee and have drinks or something. Then the first trumpet player would double on piano. And I'd take over. I'd leave the band. I'd play pop tunes. The tunes of the band were like down home in Tennessee and all that kind of stuff. Because they didn't know any addiction to it. But I…

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: I played with a band called Arnold Johnson's Orchestra.

ctx.x: What dances do you remember the people doing specific, like foxtrots, tangos?

Oh, they used to, it's according to who's giving the dance. If it's a company dance or a convention dance, you know. I even played polkas. Because during the carnival season we used to put on a couple of carnival balls away from the auditorium by tourist bureaus, and they'd bring people who liked to dance the music, perhaps that we were not used to playing. But being commercial, and I was commercial, I had everything in the box. I even had Yiddish music, I even had music in five-four time for Greeks, if they…

Do you think that the orchestras are like, we're trying to talk mostly about what I was mostly concerned about was up until about 1930, if you can kind of keep that in mind. Yeah. Do you think that orchestras like Vincent Lopez, Paul Weichmann, Leo Reismann, and so forth, had much influence on what people wanted to hear here in New Orleans? I think so.
